overview: Guinea is a country on the Atlantic coast of West Africa. Its capital and largest city is Conakry. In 1958 Guinea became the first French colony in Africa to vote for independence. French is the official language. Guinea has some of the largest reserves of bauxite in the world, the ore used to make aluminium.

geography.text: Guinea is often called the 'water tower of West Africa', because great rivers including the Niger, the Senegal and the Gambia begin in its highlands. It has a coastal plain with mangroves, the Fouta Djallon plateau in the centre, savanna in the north-east and forested mountains in the south-east.

history.text: The region was part of the Mali Empire, and later the Fula state of Futa Jallon rose in the highlands. In the late 1800s Samory Touré led resistance against France. Guinea became a French colony and, in 1958, was the only French colony to vote no to France's offer of continued ties, becoming independent straight away under Ahmed Sékou Touré.

events.title: Futa Jallon
events.text: An Islamic state is founded in the highlands.

events.title: Ebola
events.text: An Ebola epidemic that began in a Guinean village spreads to its neighbours.
